metadata.title: TALIS 2018 and TALIS Starting Strong 2018 User Guide (EN)

survey_design.weight_variable_name: TCHWGT / STAFFWGT (final teacher/staff weights); BRR-Fay replicate weights (e.g., TRWGT*, SRWGT*, CRWGT*)
survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The user guide documents that TALIS 2018 and TALIS Starting Strong 2018 are complex, multi-stage stratified cluster surveys with teachers/staff nested within schools/centres. It instructs analysts to use the provided sampling weights to compute population estimates (TCHWGT for TALIS 2018 teacher analyses; STAFFWGT for TALIS Starting Strong 2018 staff analyses) and to account for the complex design when estimating sampling errors. For variance estimation, it specifies the use of Fay’s variation of balanced repeated replication (BRR) and the corresponding replicate weights (e.g., TRWGT* for teachers, SRWGT* for staff, CRWGT* for centres). The guide also notes that some software (e.g., SPSS base module) does not fully support the required replication-based variance estimation, and therefore recommends using the IEA IDB Analyzer and the Stata repest routine to ensure correct handling of replicate weights.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a user guide/codebook describing variable content, weighting, and variance estimation procedures rather than an empirical analysis predicting a cognitive outcome. As such, it does not report a specific plausible-values (PV) strategy or a missing-data handling method for an estimated model. The guide focuses on how to analyse the released TALIS/TALIS Starting Strong databases correctly (weights and replication), while detailed PV and missing-data procedures are deferred to the associated technical reports and scale construction chapters.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The guide describes the sampling frames and participation/adjudication rules rather than providing an analytic student-level dataset. For TALIS 2018, it specifies that teachers are sampled within participating schools using a two-stage stratified cluster design, with minimum participation standards (e.g., at least 75% of sampled schools and 75% teacher participation within schools after replacement) and post-facto exclusions/adjudication for specific contexts (e.g., ultra-orthodox schools removed in Israel; Moscow excluded in Russia; some regions excluded in Saudi Arabia; participation standards not met for certain ISCED levels in Australia and the Netherlands). For TALIS Starting Strong 2018, it specifies a two-stage stratified cluster design for centres and staff, with minimum participation standards (e.g., at least 75% of sampled centres and 75% staff participation within centres) and notes that Denmark U3 and ISCED level 02 did not meet participation requirements and are set as not meeting adjudication requirements.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD user guide documents the content and format of the TALIS 2018 and TALIS Starting Strong 2018 international databases and provides practical instructions for secondary analysis. It explains that both studies are observational, cross-sectional surveys with teachers/staff nested within schools/centres, and therefore require the use of sampling weights and replication-based variance estimation. For TALIS 2018, it describes a two-stage stratified cluster sampling approach for schools and probabilistic sampling of teachers, with minimum participation standards and country-specific adjudication rules. For TALIS Starting Strong 2018, it describes a similar two-stage stratified cluster design for centres and staff, including separate questionnaire versions for ISCED 02 and U3 populations. The guide emphasizes correct handling of Fay’s variation of BRR using replicate weights and recommends the IEA IDB Analyzer and Stata repest to reproduce international-report tables, while warning that causal inferences cannot be made from these data alone.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This document is a methodological user guide and codebook rather than an empirical research article estimating a model with reported predictive performance. Consequently, there is no single dependent variable, no ML algorithm training/evaluation, and no reported PV or missing-data handling strategy for an analysis pipeline. The guide instead provides instructions for analysts to apply the provided weights and replicate weights when conducting their own analyses on the released TALIS/TALIS Starting Strong databases.
